stories.title: Claude can now analyze your spending with its new Personal Finance tool
stories.summary: With Personal Finance in Claude, users can connect their bank and card accounts through Plaid and ask questions about their finances.

sources.name: TechCrunch AI
sources.title: Claude can now analyze your spending with its new Personal Finance tool
sources.text: Anthropic announced Thursday that Claude is getting a new tool called “Personal Finance,” designed to help users keep track of their money. With it, users can connect their bank and credit card accounts through Plaid and ask Claude questions about their finances. Anthropic says access is read-only, meaning Personal Finance can’t move, manage, or invest users’ money. By letting Claude connect directly to bank and credit card accounts, Anthropic is positioning its chatbot as a financial companion that can help people understand their spending and make sense of their money, rather than simply offering them generic advice. With the launch, Claude is playing catch-up to OpenAI’s ChatGPT, which introduced similar personal finance tools in May that also let users connect their financial accounts and ask questions about everything from spending patterns to long-term financial planning. “Claude gives you answers in everyday language, from your balances and transactions, and explains any term that’s new to you,” Anthropic wrote in a blog post. “Like the rest of Claude, Personal Finance has no ads or sponsored recommendations, and it doesn’t offer credit cards, loans, or savings accounts of its own, so your money questions get a straight answer.” For instance, at the end of the month, a user could ask Claude, “Where did my money go this month?” The chatbot will then add up spending across the connected accounts and sort it by category, such as rent and utilities, food and drink, and shopping. Users can choose to go deeper by following up with questions like, “Is that more than usual?” or “Anything else I’m missing?” Anthropic says the tool goes beyond basic spending summaries by analyzing transactions across connected accounts to flag potential issues, such as duplicate charges, unexpected fees, and steadily increasing bills. Users can also ask broader questions about their finances, such as whether they’re spending more than they earn. The tool can also explain financial concepts like APR (annual percentage rate), while providing calculations that show users how much they’ve paid in interest over the past year. Of course, some people will have reservations about connecting their financial accounts to an AI chatbot. Anthropic says Claude’s access is limited to each connected bank’s name, account name and type, the last four digits of the account number, balances, credit limits, and up to two years of transaction history. Additionally, the company notes that when users chat with Claude in the Personal Finance hub, those conversations aren’t used to train its models. Personal Finance starts rolling out in beta this week to users on the Pro, Max, and Ultra plans in the U.S. The launch of the new tool comes as Anthropic has been expanding Claude into new verticals. For instance, Anthropic launched Claude for Legal and Claude for Financial Services earlier this year. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . sources.name: The Verge AI
sources.title: Claude AI can plug directly into your bank account
sources.text: With access to your bank account via Plaid, Anthropic’s chatbot will try to explain where your money is going and what you can afford.﻿ With access to your bank account via Plaid, Anthropic’s chatbot will try to explain where your money is going and what you can afford.﻿ Anthropic has a new pitch for managing your personal finances: let Claude do it instead, with a new Personal Finance feature that connects it to your bank and card accounts via the Plaid bank bridging platform. You can ask the chatbot “where did my money go this month,” for example, and it’ll create an overview with a breakdown of spending by category, including rent and utilities, shopping, and food. Claude can also answer broader questions around what bills are left before your next payday, if you can afford big purchases like holiday trips, and how much money you could be saving each month. Its access is read-only, and with Plaid facilitating the connection, Claude doesn’t see your banking passwords and your bank doesn’t have to deal with unvetted AI bots crawling around your accounts . Claude can’t move, manage, or invest your money, according to Anthropic, and it “isn’t designed to give investment advice.”, but it can see the bank’s name, account names, account type, the last four digits of the number associated with it, your balances and credit limits, and up to two years’ worth of your transaction history. If you choose to give it access to all that, Claude can explain financial terms you don’t understand and answer questions about your balances and transactions. Personal Finance in Claude is rolling out in beta this week to Claude Pro, Max, and Ultra plan subscribers in the US. Anthropic’s announcement follows OpenAI introducing a similar feature for ChatGPT in May, which also plugs into your bank accounts through Plaid. Allowing AI to have oversight into your finances might ring some alarm bells, but according to the sign-off in Anthropic’s press release, it’s just the beginning: “Personal Finance is a first step. For life’s bigger money decisions, we think people are best served by Claude working alongside the licensed professionals and regulated firms they trust. We’re exploring how to make that possible in Claude, and we’d like to hear from banks, wealth managers, and financial services companies who want to help shape it.”

sources.name: ZDNet AI
sources.title: Claude’s new Personal Finance tool aims to help analyze your spending – read-only, of course
sources.text: Anthropic has released what appears to be its answer to ChatGPT Finances. You can now share your financial information with Claude and ask the chatbot for insights on your spending. Also: Researchers asked people to use AI chatbots for election info Personal Finance in Claude, which Anthropic announced Thursday, reviews your connected accounts through read-only access via Plaid. That security measure follows OpenAI’s equivalent feature, ChatGPT Finances , which launched in May. Here’s what to know. Functionally, this feature appears similar to ChatGPT Finances: It lets you link as many bank and credit card accounts as you’d like to Claude via Plaid with read-only access. You can then ask Claude where you spent your money this month or whether you can afford to take a vacation in six months, for example. (Disclosure: Ziff Davis, ZDNET’s parent company, filed an April 2025 lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.) Also: Stop sharing your passwords with AI agents According to Anthropic, the feature is a response to existing use patterns: the company’s April usage report found that financial advice was one of the main topics users ask Claude for help with. Given the privacy concerns around sharing sensitive data with AI systems, especially agents, Anthropic emphasized which data the new feature will access and how. “For the accounts you choose to connect (and only those), Claude sees the bank’s name, each account’s name, type, and last four digits, balances and credit limits, and up to two years of transactions. When you chat with Claude in the Personal Finance hub, those conversations aren’t used to train our models.” That last part is important: Personal Finance in Claude is its own mode with its own protections. If you share or discuss your financial data with Claude outside that “hub,” it’s subject only to your Claude privacy settings. The idea behind the feature is that you can ask follow-up questions and request more insights about spending habits, trends over time, and future goals based on what Claude finds, similar to any other Claude conversation. The tool will also generate tables and charts to visualize your financial information. “You can ask for a weekly spending chart, a calendar of what’s due, or a dashboard of the numbers you choose, and Claude builds it as an artifact you can keep adjusting and coming back to,” an Anthropic representative told ZDNET via email. Also: I connected ChatGPT to my bank, and it’s my go-to finance app now You can also expect an ad-free experience in the feature. “Like the rest of Claude, Personal Finance has no ads or sponsored recommendations, and it doesn’t offer credit cards, loans, or savings accounts of its own, so your money questions get a straight answer,” the company said in the announcement. The company added that because Claude is using actual transaction data and not memory, the feature shouldn’t hallucinate. “It can list the exact transactions behind any number so you can check its math,” Anthropic said via email. “Like any AI, it can make mistakes, so for anything important, we recommend confirming with your bank.” For now, Personal Finance in Claude is available only to Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers in the US. Given the many finance apps out there, it may primarily be for users who already use Claude for much of their work and day-to-day and don’t want to switch interfaces. Still, the difference — and for many, the appeal — here is the natural language interface. Other finance apps don’t necessarily have an easy, accessible chat function where users can shoot off quick questions like they would to a human financial planner. These assistants also present historical budget analysis in plain English, rather than requiring users to interpret dashboards themselves, which users may see as a perk. Also: 5 ways to use AI when your budget is tight On Reddit, many users find ChatGPT Finances to be accurate and reliable. One Reddit user said ChatGPT Finance seemed to have Mint or Monarch potential, but noted it was still “weaker” than those apps in some areas, such as historical syncing, high-quality dashboards, and generating full statement PDFs. ZDNET editor-in-chief Elyse Betters Picaro was “incredibly impressed” with ChatGPT Finances when she tried it out , and still uses it as one of several financial tools (not a replacement for professional advice). She also has her privacy settings in ChatGPT structured to reduce any security risks. “ChatGPT has genuinely helped me make better financial decisions,” she wrote. Anthropic noted that users shouldn’t look to Personal Finance for Claude as a total authority. “Personal Finance is a first step. For life’s bigger money decisions, we think people are best served by Claude working alongside the licensed professionals and regulated firms they trust,” the company said in the announcement. “We’re exploring how to make that possible in Claude, and we’d like to hear from banks, wealth managers, and financial services companies who want to help shape it” — indicating a more integrated financial planning system within Claude may be on the way. sources.name: Engadget
sources.title: Now Claude can help with your finances too
sources.text: Anthropic has begun testing a new personal finance experience inside of Claude. Starting this week, Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers in the US can connect their financial accounts to Claude in order to get personalized financial advice from the chatbot. Like OpenAI did with ChatGPT Finances in May , Anthropic has partnered with Plaid to allow users to connect their bank accounts. Plaid's backend has connections to more than 12,000 financial institutions, including many major US banks like Citi and Chase. When you connect a financial account to Claude, Anthropic notes the chatbot will be limited to read-only access. "Personal Finance can't move, manage or invest your money," the company says, adding it didn't design the tool to give people investment advice, and that Claude can only access up to two years of transactions. Anthropic is also quick to distance its offering from OpenAI's, pointing to the company's ad policy . "Personal Finance has no ads or sponsored recommendations, and it doesn't offer credit cards, loans or savings accounts of its own, so your money questions get a straight answer," Anthropic says. Additionally, the company says it won't use any conversations you have inside the Personal Finance hub for model training. "For anything you share with Claude outside the hub, your privacy settings apply," it adds. Again, this is different from OpenAI, which applies your existing data control settings to ChatGPT's personal finance experience, meaning if you don't modify them, you're enrolled in model training by default. Outside of those differences, the two tools appear to offer broadly the same features. You can ask Claude to look through your accounts to spot unexpected fees, double-charges and any monthly bills that have gone up over the year. It can also generate weekly spending charts, expense calendars and budget breakdowns. And if there are any terms you're not familiar with, like say APR, you can ask Claude to explain those too. Looking forward, Anthropic says it's exploring how Claude can work alongside licensed professionals and regulated firms to offer financial advice. Just what that might look like, the company doesn't say, but it's asking that banks and wealth managers get in touch. The timing of today's announcement probably has a lot to do with Anthropic's impending IPO , which the company is expected to complete sometime in the next few weeks.

stories.title: ChatGPT ganha ferramenta para criar e editar GIFs
stories.summary: Além de criar animações, a ferramenta permite ajustar a velocidade de reprodução, editar quadros individuais e compartilhar o resultado O post ChatGPT ganha ferramenta para criar e editar GIFs apareceu primeiro em Olhar Digital .

sources.name: Olhar Digital IA
sources.title: ChatGPT ganha ferramenta para criar e editar GIFs
sources.text: O ChatGPT ganhou novidade que pode facilitar a criação de conteúdo para redes sociais: a capacidade de produzir GIFs animados diretamente na plataforma. Com a atualização, usuários podem descrever a animação desejada em um comando de texto ou enviar uma fotografia para transformá-la em conteúdo animado. A novidade acompanha o lançamento do Images 2.6, nova versão do gerador de imagens da OpenAI . Além de criar animações, a ferramenta permite ajustar a velocidade de reprodução, editar quadros individuais e compartilhar o resultado. Até então, o ChatGPT não oferecia maneira nativa de produzir GIFs em uma única etapa. Era necessário recorrer a ferramentas externas ou realizar procedimentos adicionais para transformar imagens em animações. A OpenAI demonstrou o recurso com um comando simples: pedir ao chatbot que criasse um GIF de um gato dançando. O sistema produz a animação e oferece controles para modificar sua velocidade e visualizar os quadros que compõem o resultado. A atualização também contempla desenvolvedores. A OpenAI apresentou duas opções de modelos para geração de imagens por meio da API: As duas opções ampliam as possibilidades de integração da tecnologia em aplicativos e outros serviços digitais. O Images 2.6 está sendo disponibilizado para usuários do ChatGPT e do Codex nas versões web, desktop e aplicativos para dispositivos móveis. A distribuição ocorre de maneira gradual, portanto, a novidade pode não aparecer simultaneamente para todas as contas. Com a possibilidade de criar e editar animações diretamente no chatbot, a OpenAI amplia o alcance de suas ferramentas visuais. O recurso pode ser útil para produzir memes, ilustrações animadas, materiais de divulgação e conteúdos para redes sociais sem precisar alternar entre diferentes aplicativos. A mudança também reforça a estratégia da empresa de transformar o ChatGPT em plataforma de criação de conteúdo, indo além das tradicionais conversas por texto. Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

sources.title: ChatGPT agora cria GIFs com o nova IA Images 2.6
sources.text: Dots x Muse: Qual o Melhor Agente de IA em 2026? Dots da OpenAI ou Muse da Meta: qual ecossistema de agentes de IA vale mais a pena?. Crédito: Pedro Castro A OpenAI anunciou, na quarta-feira (4), o Images 2.6, novo modelo de geração de imagens do ChatGPT. Além de gerar imagens com maior velocidade, a nova inteligência artificial pode criar GIFs sem precisar de ferramentas adicionais. O Images 2.6 da OpenAI traz melhorias na velocidade de geração e no controle das criações . Segundo a empresa, a tecnologia produz imagens 50% mais rápido do que as versões anteriores e oferece maior precisão durante as edições. Na API, o novo modelo está disponível em duas versões: o GPT-Image-2.6 Flare é projetado para criar imagens mais rapidamente, priorizando a velocidade; o GPT-Image-2.6 Sunburst, por sua vez, é voltado para trabalhos que exigem maior nível de detalhes, precisão e consistência entre edições. Segundo a OpenAI, os usuários já criam mais de 4 bilhões de imagens por semana no ChatGPT, Codex e API , superando os 3 bilhões semanais reportados anteriormente. A atualização também dá ao ChatGPT a capacidade de criar GIFs nativamente , sem depender de ferramentas externas. A IA gera uma sequência de imagens para proporcionar a sensação de movimento, permitindo ao usuário ajustar a velocidade da animação e editar quadros individuais após a produção. O Images 2.6 foi liberado globalmente no ChatGPT e no Codex, nas versões web, desktop e mobile, para todos os planos. Os modelos GPT-Image-2.6 Flare e Sunburst também estão disponíveis na API da OpenAI. Quer ficar por dentro das novidades do mundo da tecnologia? sources.name: Canaltech
sources.title: ChatGPT agora cria GIFs animados direto no chat e permite editar quadros
sources.text: O ChatGPT ganhou um recurso nativo para criar GIFs animados a partir de texto ou imagens enviadas pelos usuários. A novidade faz parte do modelo Images 2.6, lançado pela OpenAI, que está disponível globalmente no ChatGPT e no Codex para todos os usuários, incluindo versões para navegador, computador e celulares. A tecnologia também chegou à API para desenvolvedores. Com a atualização, é possível criar GIFs e editar as animações em uma única etapa e sem sair da conversa. Assim, é possível animar mascotes e personagens de marcas, transformar fotos de produtos em sequências que se repetem continuamente, criar storyboards animados e dar movimento a esboços feitos à mão. A interface também oferece controles para alterar a velocidade de reprodução, visualizar os quadros individualmente e editar cenas. A velocidade pode variar de 0,5x a 2x. O Images 2.6 também traz melhorias no desempenho. Segundo a OpenAI, o modelo gera imagens 50% mais rápido do que a versão anterior. A empresa afirma que seus usuários criam mais de 4 bilhões de imagens por semana no ChatGPT, Codex e API. Em setembro, o volume registrado era de 3 bilhões semanais. A atualização também chegou à API da OpenAI , que recebeu duas variantes do modelo. O GPT-Image-2.6 Flare prioriza a velocidade, com geração de imagens em até seis segundos na configuração de baixa qualidade, e foi otimizado para criar pôsteres, fotos de produtos e materiais profissionais com melhor qualidade de layout. Já o GPT-Image-2.6 Sunburst oferece maior precisão e consistência, principalmente nas configurações de qualidade média e alta. Além disso, a API ganhou suporte à exportação de arquivos SVG e à marcação de imagens , recurso que já estava disponível no ChatGPT e agora também pode ser usado por desenvolvedores. A OpenAI ainda adicionou parâmetros para controlar a qualidade das imagens e a complexidade do planejamento das cenas. A criação de GIFs acontece na própria conversa com o ChatGPT. É necessário apenas descrever a animação desejada ou enviar uma imagem para servir de referência. Depois da geração, a interface apresenta controles para personalizar o resultado, como: Velocidade : ajuste da reprodução entre 0,5x, 0,75x, 1x, 1,25x, 1,5x, 1,75x e 2x; Visualização dos quadros : abertura de uma tela com a sequência completa de imagens que compõem o GIF; Edição : alteração de detalhes visuais dos quadros; Comentários : inclusão de observações sobre a imagem; Redimensionamento : ajuste das dimensões e da proporção do arquivo; Remoção : exclusão de elementos ou quadros da animação. Quando terminar os ajustes, o usuário pode baixar ou compartilhar o arquivo do GIF. Se você gostou do conteúdo, talvez também se interesse por conferir “ 7 melhores IAs para gerar imagens além do ChatGPT e Gemini ”.

stories.title: Eleição nos EUA expõe reação a bilionários e data centers de IA
stories.summary: Data centers de IA, custo de vida e corrupção pesaram na eleição dos EUA, que deu aos democratas o controle das duas casas do Congresso O post Eleição nos EUA expõe reação a bilionários e data centers de IA apareceu primeiro em Olhar Digital .

sources.name: Olhar Digital IA
sources.title: Eleição nos EUA expõe reação a bilionários e data centers de IA
sources.text: Os democratas conquistaram o controle do Congresso dos Estados Unidos nas eleições de meio de mandato de 2026, impondo uma derrota ao presidente Donald Trump e aos candidatos apoiados por grandes empresários do setor de tecnologia. O resultado reflete a insatisfação dos eleitores com o custo de vida, a corrupção e a expansão dos data centers de inteligência artificial (IA). Também representa um revés para bilionários que investiram centenas de milhões de dólares nas campanhas republicanas. No Texas, James Talarico derrotou Ken Paxton e se tornou o primeiro democrata eleito para o Senado pelo estado em quase quatro décadas. Na disputa pelo governo estadual, Gina Hinojosa venceu Greg Abbott, que estava no cargo havia três mandatos. Ela será a primeira governadora democrata do Texas desde Ann Richards, que deixou o posto em 1995. A derrota também atingiu candidatos escolhidos pessoalmente por Trump, que havia feito dezenas de endossos durante a campanha. O resultado no Texas ganhou destaque em meio à resistência de parte dos eleitores à expansão da infraestrutura tecnológica. Hinojosa defendeu a suspensão de novos projetos de data centers até que regras mais rigorosas sejam adotadas. A preocupação com essas instalações apareceu em uma pesquisa da CNBC : 56% dos entrevistados disseram que a questão teve importância decisiva ou significativa na escolha de seus candidatos. A derrota republicana também representa um revés para empresários e grupos de interesse que financiaram candidatos favoráveis à expansão da infraestrutura de inteligência artificial . Elon Musk , o maior doador individual do ciclo eleitoral e o homem mais rico do mundo, gastou valores recordes para tentar manter os republicanos no poder. No Texas, investiu mais de US$ 200 milhões (cerca de R$ 1,08 bilhão) em esforços para impedir a vitória de Talarico. O peso desse financiamento aparece também no perfil dos principais doadores: 14 dos 20 maiores grupos apoiaram exclusivamente ou quase exclusivamente candidatos republicanos. Interesses ligados a criptomoedas , inteligência artificial e jogos de azar on-line investiram mais de US$ 377 milhões (aproximadamente R$ 2,04 bilhões). Com a conquista da maioria na Câmara e no Senado, os democratas terão mais poder para fiscalizar o governo Trump, convocar autoridades e abrir investigações. Parlamentares já defenderam chamar executivos de empresas de inteligência artificial para depor sob juramento. A mudança no equilíbrio político também põe em xeque as tentativas republicanas de redesenhar distritos eleitorais para favorecer seus candidatos. Democratas venceram disputas em áreas do Texas, da Flórida e da Carolina do Norte cujos limites haviam sido alterados com esse objetivo. Outras vitórias ampliaram o alcance da mudança no mapa eleitoral: os democratas venceram disputas na Carolina do Sul, em Ohio, na Geórgia e em New Hampshire, além de conquistar cadeiras no Senado em Iowa e na Carolina do Norte. A insatisfação econômica teve papel central na eleição. Muitos eleitores atribuíram a piora das condições econômicas às tarifas impostas por Trump e à guerra contra o Irã. Uma pesquisa da CNBC realizada em outubro apontou a corrupção como a principal preocupação dos entrevistados. Após a divulgação dos resultados, os contratos futuros dos índices Dow Jones e S&P 500 recuaram. Com o novo controle do Congresso, os democratas poderão bloquear parte da agenda presidencial e intensificar a fiscalização sobre o governo nos dois últimos anos do mandato de Trump. Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

sources.title: OpenAI tenta conquistar apoio popular para construir data centers nos EUA
sources.text: OS DATA CENTERS PODEM PREJUDICAR O PARTIDO DE TRUMP NAS ELEIÇÕES DOS EUA? O repórter do Estadão, Daniel Gateno, fala sobre o documentário “Estadão na América”, que estreia nesta semana, e o medo dos americanos com o futuro dos Estados. A OpenAI iniciou, nesta quinta-feira (5), uma nova campanha para tentar melhorar a imagem dos data centers de inteligência artificial perante a população dos Estados Unidos . A iniciativa ganhou importância após as eleições de meio de mandato que tiveram o Partido Democrata obtendo vitórias expressivas, inclusive em estados considerados essenciais para a construção dessas instalações. O objetivo é reduzir a rejeição popular contra os planos da indústria de IA de erguer novos centros de dados em todo o país. Para tanto, as políticas atualizadas da startup preveem uma maior aproximação com as comunidades que receberão a infraestrutura, mostrando como a obra pode beneficiar os moradores . Uma das estratégias que a dona do ChatGPT passa a adotar é não usar mais acordos de confidencialidade com autoridades públicas ao negociar possíveis locais para futuras instalações. A empresa afirma que isso tornará as conversas mais transparentes, reduzindo a desconfiança em torno do negócio. Segundo Chris Lehane, diretor de assuntos globais da OpenAI, uma instalação que funcionará no estado de Ohio vai gerar cerca de 2.500 empregos de longo prazo. O salário médio anual oferecido aos contratados será de US$ 80.000 , o equivalente a cerca de R$ 438.000 pela cotação atual. “Esses projetos não são o tipo de data center que as pessoas imaginavam, que eram uma espécie de caixa-preta em um pasto , que contribuíam muito pouco em termos de utilidade econômica para os comunidades onde estavam localizados”, disse o porta-voz da companhia, durante coletiva. A nova estratégia da startup também será primordial para lidar com as mudanças no cenário político do país. Candidatos que prometeram barrar novas licenças para data centers foram eleitos em estados como Texas, Ohio e Georgia , o que pode afetar os planos da indústria de IA. Um dos trunfos da OpenAI é o próprio Lehane, que afirmou ter uma “vasta experiência” com os Democratas ao ser questionado sobre como lidaria com as restrições aos data centers defendidas por alguns membros do partido. Ele trabalhou como porta-voz do governo de Bill Clinton e na campanha do vice-presidente, Al Gore. Como parte da iniciativa, a empresa decidiu renomear seus centros de dados. sources.title: Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
sources.text: Some of the largest AI infrastructure projects in the world are underway in Texas. A dramatic political shift could slow their construction—and deepen concerns about the economics of the AI boom. Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech's largest AI buildouts. But the blue wave that swept the Lone Star State may jeopardize that position. Democrat James Talarico won the US Senate seat against Ken Paxton. Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor against the Republican incumbent, Greg Abbott. At the state level, Democrats will take control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years. Talarico and Hinojosa made data centers a central issue, discussing them constantly on the campaign trail. Even before the polls closed, insiders in the data center industry noticed that the times were changing. At the industry's DCD conference in Ashburn, Virginia, on Tuesday, panelists lamented that Texas had been the easiest place to build for years—until September. That's when Abbott, perhaps seeing the increasingly bipartisan distaste for these facilities , began changing course himself. Developers said the governor’s office had stopped responding to their emails. On September 21, Abbott directed a key state regulator to halt data center permits. Many panelists at the conference were expecting this to mean that existing projects might be slowed and new ones could be halted altogether. The governor-elect indeed seems eager to do that. Hinojosa supported tax breaks for data centers in 2023 as a way to boost construction jobs, but during her campaign she began pushing for a full-fledged moratorium. That would be a problem for the hyperscalers of Big Tech, which have ambitious plans for AI training facilities in the state. The scale of projects already underway in Texas is massive. The Stargate Frontier data center in Shackelford County is projected to serve 1,820 megawatts—about as much as the nation’s largest data center, SpaceX’s Colossus 2 in Tennessee, and more than twice as much as the largest data center currently operating in Texas. Nexus Hubbard, also under construction and intended mostly to serve Anthropic, has a planned size of 6,400 megawatts and is the second-largest data center being built in the US, behind only Meta’s Hyperion project in Louisiana. The potential for Democrats to order delays to these projects or moratoriums on new ones adds to growing anxiety that the AI buildout could stall. Banks and lenders are already getting pickier about the projects they back. And given the extent to which the data center buildout is underpinning growth in the economy right now, those forces combined could have ripple effects. Voters around the country, though, were unambiguous in the midterms, sending a similar message on everything from state ballot questions to national offices. Voters supported efforts to protect ratepayers from increases in their electricity bills caused by data centers, and they favored some larger bans on new data centers altogether. If we needed any more convincing that Big Tech has fumbled its effort to sell voters on the idea that AI-powered abundance will make health care better, goods cheaper, and scientific breakthroughs more common, this was it. A key question is whether the Texas counties with the largest data center presence were part of the reason these Democrats got elected, or if the anti-data-center vote came from elsewhere. It’s complicated: The counties where much of the data center buildout is happening are around Dallas. Dallas County and others closest to it predictably went blue, but nearby Ellis County, which leads in permitting requests for data centers, went for Greg Abbott and Ken Paxton. Cameron County, near the state’s southern border, is a hot spot for data centers and voted blue in the midterms, which was a shift. But Mitchell County and Scurry County, where a bunch of projects in west Texas are located, went red. This is a big deal, because no single office in the state decides whether a project goes ahead or is halted. Decisions often reflect an interplay between city governments, county officials, and state offices. Local officials who have some say over data center development may resist sweeping restrictions from the state. And Democrats pushing for a moratorium might also face pushback from the construction unions that supported some of their campaigns. So while the blue wave spells a death knell for Texas data centers in theory, election winners may find that following through on their opposition once in office is much more complicated than campaigning on it. Ten years after AlphaGo’s match against Go champion Lee Sedol, today’s AI still isn’t tapping into the machinery that made that win possible. An exclusive interview with Nick Cammarata, the researcher whose 26,000-word viral blog post has AI safety folks celebrating. Breathless claims about AGI and new capabilities fall apart pretty quickly under scrutiny. Surveillance towers, increasingly powered by AI, promised faster responses to crossings. Our investigation of deaths near the towers found they are failing to deliver. Discover special offers, top stories, upcoming events, and more.

sources.name: Fortune
sources.title: Elon Musk spent at least $225 million in Texas. The governor-elect who sued for Abbott emails and vowed a data center freeze won anyway
sources.text: Elon Musk directed at least $225 million of his midterm spending to Texas, according to OpenSecrets data NPR reported . Texas is home to the headquarters of Tesla and SpaceX, and on Tuesday its voters handed Democrats the governor’s office, a U.S. Senate seat, and the state House anyway. Democrat Gina Hinojosa unseated three-term Gov. Greg Abbott , becoming the state’s first Latina governor and ending a Republican hold on the office that began in 1995. James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton , the first Democratic U.S. Senate win in Texas since 1988. Democrats also won control of the Texas House for the first time since Republicans took it in 2002. For Musk, the result replaces a governor who championed his Texas expansion with one who sued to see Abbott’s communications with him and has promised to freeze data center approvals. Tesla, SpaceX, and Terafab, the $16.8 billion chip plant they are building in Grimes County, all depend on state cooperation for their next phase in Texas. Musk gave more than $445 million to Republican candidates, PACs, and outside groups this cycle, making him the top donor of the midterms, according to OpenSecrets; other tallies run higher. Since May 2025, he has given more to federal political groups than George Soros has personally given in his lifetime, a Fortune analysis found . Texas hosts Tesla’s Austin headquarters and Gigafactory, SpaceX’s Starbase launch site, and X, which became part of SpaceX when SpaceX merged with xAI in February. Tesla, a Fortune 500 company , is unlikely to see immediate manufacturing disruptions. It could face more scrutiny of its Autopilot and Full Self-Driving technology and its planned Cybercab robotaxi rollout, especially with Democrats also winning both chambers of Congress . Democratic lawmakers could also push for a closer look at Musk’s companies and their government relationships. SpaceX’s Texas expansion and its AI infrastructure ambitions could meet tougher environmental reviews and more contentious debates over electricity, water, and data center development. Hinojosa has made that fight central. “I will issue a moratorium — a ban — on all data center approvals,” she said in an Oct. 22 video, pledging to keep it in place until the Legislature passes new protections, the Texas Tribune reported . Abbott himself paused new data center permits in September pending a grid audit. The open question for Musk is how long, and how broadly, a Hinojosa freeze would apply. Terafab’s first phase represents a capital investment of more than $16.8 billion and is expected to create 3,000 jobs, according to Abbott’s office . The full project could be built in up to four phases at a total cost of $55 billion to $119 billion, Manufacturing Dive reported . The state has extended a $30 million Texas Enterprise Fund grant, and the plant qualifies for the Jobs, Energy, Technology, and Innovation (JETI) program, which reduces school property taxes for large projects. The election doesn’t automatically cancel those commitments, but closer scrutiny of incentives and environmental requirements could raise costs or slow later phases. Terafab is a chip plant, not a conventional data center. Its energy and infrastructure demands could still draw attention from officials concerned about industrial expansion, and Musk has said the facility will produce AI chips at scale . Hinojosa challenged Abbott’s relationship with Musk before she won. On Oct. 19, the first day of early voting, she sued for access to unredacted communications between Abbott’s office and Musk and his companies. Her lawsuit says the governor’s office described some of those records as “intimate and embarrassing.” She pointed to a $1.66 billion JETI tax break tied to Terafab , more than $54 million in state grants to SpaceX, and Abbott’s push for the state broadband office to award Starlink $110 million upfront from federal funds, a move that triggered an audit of the office . Abbott’s office called the suit “a baseless stunt.” State District Judge Catherine Mauzy ordered Abbott’s office on Oct. 26 to let Hinojosa inspect the records, and the 15th Court of Appeals stayed that order the next day . Bloomberg Government separately reported that Mauzy had donated $500 to Hinojosa’s campaign in June. Starting in January, Hinojosa will control state appointments, the veto, and the governor’s office that administers the Texas Enterprise Fund. Republicans kept their 19-12 majority in the Texas Senate , but Democrat Vikki Goodwin’s win in the lieutenant governor’s race gives the party the chamber’s presiding officer. Shares of Musk’s two public companies fell the day after the election while the broader market rose. Tesla closed down 3.3% and SpaceX down 3.8% on Nov. 4, according to Yahoo Finance. The timing doesn’t prove investors were reacting to Texas. But Wells Fargo’s chief equity strategist, Ohsung Kwon, had warned that a Democratic win in the governor’s race could be a “left-tail event” for the AI trade, CNBC reported . Musk is also weighing a merger of Tesla and SpaceX, a deal that Democratic majorities in Congress could now scrutinize. Fortune has reported on what the merger talks reveal about his power . Hinojosa takes office in January, the same month lawmakers return to Austin. The next tests are how far her data center freeze reaches, whether Terafab’s JETI agreements draw legislative review, and whether the fight over Abbott’s Musk records outlasts his administration.

stories.title: Sony vuelve a los ochenta con los MDR-3R, una versión modernizada de los auriculares para Walkman
stories.summary: La compañía japonesa ha reinterpretado los MDR-3 originales con un formato moderno y fiel al original, USB-C, micrófono integrado y un botón en el cable para llamadas.

sources.name: Computer Hoy
sources.title: Sony vuelve a los ochenta con los MDR-3R, una versión modernizada de los auriculares para Walkman
sources.text: Elígenos como tu fuente preferida en Google. La compañía japonesa ha reinterpretado los MDR-3 originales con un formato moderno y fiel al original, USB-C, micrófono integrado y un botón en el cable para llamadas. Sony acaba de anunciar los MDR-3R, una reinterpretación de sus clásicos auriculares de los ochenta Walkman MDR-3, que vienen con cable USB-C, un micrófono integrado para llamadas, un mando a distancia en el propio cable para colgar el teléfono. Su precio es de 59 euros y, por el momento, no se ha concretado cuándo se pondrán a la venta en España, pero sí se ha avanzado que contarán con una versión adicional inspirada en Stranger Things. La empresa tecnológica nipona lanzó estos auriculares en 1979, junto con el Walkman, contribuyendo a crear una nueva manera de disfrutar de la música con total libertad y en cualquier lugar; una esencia que ahora quiere recuperar con un formato adaptado a los tiempos actuales. Los auriculares MDR-3R heredan el concepto de los originales, los MDR-3, de modo que están diseñados para que los usuarios puedan disfrutar de música y otros contenidos con total liberad en cualquier lugar, ya sea en interiores o al aire libre. De ese modo, conservan el diseño original , que refleja la tradición de la cultura audio portátil, al tiempo que incorporan características modernas de usabilidad. Entre ellas, la conectividad USB-C, sin interrupciones, un micrófono integrado para llamadas y un mano a distancia en el cable. Lo que sí que se mantienen son sus emblemáticas almohadillas azules y naranjas, gracias a lo cual los usuarios podrán mostrar su estado de ánimo o sus preferencias con ellas. Y, lo mejor de todo, es que el embalaje y el manual de instrucciones del modelo de los ochenta también se ha reproducido en esta ocasión. Los MDR-3R también recrean un diseño ligero y abierto, proporcionando una comodidad duradera incluso en sesiones de escucha prolongadas. Además, fomentan el plug-and-play para conectarlos rápidamente a los dispositivos compatibles y escuchar música, sin tener que cargarlos previamente o emparejarlos. También emplean los mismos transductores de sus predecesores, de 23 mm, para reproducir una calidad de sonido cercana a la original. No obstante, aunque se mantiene fiel a la firma sonora original, se han incorporado mejoras para adaptarse a las preferencias auditivas de la actualidad. Junto con la versión original, Sony ha anunciado el lanzamiento de una edición especial de estos auriculares , coincidiendo con la gran popularidad que ha tenido y aún conserva Stranger Things, una de las principales producciones de Netflix. Estos MDR-3 edición Stranger Things cuenta con detalles de diseño exclusivos, como es el caso del logotipo de la producción grabado en la diadema y un embalaje personalizado, que amplía la experiencia más allá de los propios auriculares.

sources.name: Xataka
sources.title: Sony revive los auriculares del Walkman de 1979 con los nuevos MDR-3R y se suma al regreso del audio con cable
sources.text: Hay algo curioso en el momento tecnológico que vivimos. Tenemos teléfonos capaces de hacer fotografías excelentes y, aun así, las cámaras digitales compactas vuelven a despertar interés ; llevamos años escuchando música por Bluetooth, pero los auriculares con cable también están recuperando atractivo . No son necesariamente pasos atrás. A veces buscamos una estética concreta, otras veces preferimos objetos sencillos o queremos prescindir de una batería más. En medio de tantas novedades, algunas ideas del pasado están encontrando una segunda vida, y el audio portátil es un buen ejemplo. Sony sabe muy bien lo que significa llevar la música a todas partes. En 1979 lanzó el Walkman TPS-L2 , aquel reproductor de casetes portátil que ayudó a transformar nuestros hábitos de escucha y que llegó acompañado de unos auriculares especialmente ligeros, los MDR-3L2. No eran un accesorio cualquiera, sino una parte esencial de una propuesta que permitía disfrutar de la música mientras caminábamos por la calle. Ahora, casi medio siglo después, la firma japonesa ha vuelto a mirar hacia sus orígenes para presentar los MDR-3R , unos nuevos auriculares inspirados en aquella primera generación. La recuperación no se limita al nombre. Basta con observar los MDR-3R para reconocer varios elementos de los auriculares originales : una diadema fina, la forma curvada de su estructura, las perforaciones laterales y hasta el logotipo. El fabricante mantiene una construcción abierta y ligera, con un peso de solo 38 gramos y una diadema ajustable. Hay también un detalle especialmente reconocible: las almohadillas intercambiables en azul y naranja , ambos juegos incluidos en la caja, que permiten cambiar su apariencia. El homenaje continúa en el embalaje y el manual de instrucciones, que también recuperan referencias visuales del modelo histórico. La apariencia mira al pasado, pero la forma de conectarlos responde a los dispositivos actuales. Los MDR-3R utilizan USB-C y prescinden del tradicional minijack de 3,5 milímetros , por lo que no pueden enchufarse directamente a una salida de audio analógica. El cable mide 1,2 metros e incorpora un micrófono y un mando para controlar la reproducción y gestionar las llamadas, sin baterías que recargar ni dispositivos que emparejar. Eso sí, necesitan un equipo compatible con USB Audio Class 1.0 , y Sony advierte de que algunas funciones pueden variar según el dispositivo, el sistema operativo o la aplicación. Curiosamente, tampoco recomienda utilizarlos con sus reproductores Walkman . En el apartado sonoro, los MDR-3R incorporan transductores de 23 milímetros , el mismo diámetro que los utilizados en los auriculares originales, y una configuración que, según el fabricante, busca recuperar su carácter acústico. La firma japonesa promete un sonido natural y equilibrado , especialmente en las voces, aunque reconoce haber introducido pequeños ajustes para adaptarlo a las preferencias actuales. Su construcción abierta, por otra parte, implica un aislamiento limitado frente al ruido exterior y permite que parte del sonido escape hacia fuera. Tampoco cuentan con cancelación activa de ruido, algo que conviene tener presente si pensamos utilizarlos en entornos concurridos. La mirada a los años ochenta también se extiende a una colaboración con Netflix. Sony ha anunciado una edición limitada de los MDR-3R inspirada en ' Stranger Things ', una serie cuya estética está estrechamente vinculada a aquella década. Esta versión tiene una diadema negra, incluye almohadillas intercambiables rojas y negras que recuerdan a los auriculares de Max y añade el logotipo de la producción grabado, además de un embalaje exclusivo inspirado en el Upside Down. En España, la versión convencional tiene un precio recomendado de 60 euros , frente a los 70 euros de esta edición especial. Sony sitúa la disponibilidad de ambos modelos en noviembre de 2026, sin concretar el día de lanzamiento en nuestro país. Las cifras ayudan a entender por qué el cable vuelve a encontrar su espacio. Según Circana , los ingresos por ventas de auriculares con cable aumentaron un 3% en Estados Unidos durante 2025, después de cinco años de descensos, y un 20% en las primeras seis semanas de 2026. Eso no significa que los modelos inalámbricos hayan perdido su posición dominante ni que sepamos cuánto pesará la nostalgia en las decisiones de compra. Lo interesante de la propuesta de Sony es que recupera un producto asociado a sus orígenes para ofrecerlo a consumidores que viven en un mundo tecnológico muy diferente al de 1979. Auriculares Sony MDR-3R | Diseño retro inspirado en el Walkman original | USB-C | Transductores de 23 mm | 38 gramos En Xataka | Los auriculares con cable han pasado de ser una molestia a un accesorio de moda. La clave está en lo que representan: desconexión

stories.title: OpenAI debuts new cybersecurity-focused AI model amid growing alarm about AI-driven cyber attacks
stories.summary: GPT-6 Cyber will initially be available to a small number of approved customers due to concerns that, in the wrong hands, it could supercharge cyberattacks.

sources.name: Fortune
sources.title: OpenAI debuts new cybersecurity-focused AI model amid growing alarm about AI-driven cyber attacks
sources.text: OpenAI has debuted a new AI model geared towards helping cybersecurity professionals. The company says that the new model, called GPT-6 Cyber, outperforms its general-purpose GPT-6 Astra model on most cyber tasks. Because of the risk that the model could be used to conduct cyberattacks if it fell into the wrong hands, OpenAI is current making the model available only to a small handful approved security customers. Fortune first reported that OpenAI was planning to release a specialized cyber model based on GPT-6 in September. As AI models have become better at finding software flaws and turning them into working attacks, businesses have come under increasing pressure to strengthen their cyber defenses. Gartner forecast in September that worldwide AI cybersecurity spending would reach $51.3 billion this year, nearly double last year’s $25.9 billion. OpenAI is increasingly leaning into this market, seeing it as an important path to growing its enterprise sales. This is OpenAI’s fourth cybersecurity-focused model this year, following versions released in April, June and August. The company also hired a chief revenue officer, Dali Rajic , who comes from a cybersecurity software background. Google and Anthropic are also competing for security customers. Anthropic’s Glasswing program gives vetted users access to capabilities that its public models might block. Google, which previously emphasized a lightweight, low-cost model for repeatedly scanning large codebases, has also begun offering vetted defenders access to its frontier Gemini 4 Argon model without cyber guardrails through its Fairwind Program. OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber focuses on advanced vulnerability research and exploit development. To test a server’s defenses, researchers may try breaking into it to see what an attacker could do with a flaw. The same methods can be used in malicious attacks, so general-purpose AI models impose restrictions that can also block legitimate security work. OpenAI has said it trains its Cyber models both to improve specialized cybersecurity skills and reduce refusals for certain tasks that can serve attackers and defenders. OpenAI tested GPT-6 Cyber on Firefox, Mozilla’s web browser, and the Linux kernel, the core software underlying many servers. Firefox must handle potentially malicious webpages without exposing users’ data, while the Linux kernel controls access to a machine’s resources. Both are open-source projects whose code has been inspected, tested, and hardened by developers and security researchers for years. And yet AI models are still able to find novel vulnerabilities. OpenAI says researchers used GPT-6 Cyber to find 81 previously unknown, high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities and develop working exploits for 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, including 588 previously unknown flaws. The Linux exploits could let an attacker with ordinary local access gain root privileges, the highest level of control over the system. Researchers developed working exploits for more than five times as many Linux vulnerabilities as in a July study using GPT-5.6 Sol, which was considered a state-of-the-art model for cyber tasks when it was released that month. OpenAI currently offers two levels of access to trusted cybersecurity professionals through its Daybreak program: Daybreak Red supports advanced work such as simulating attacks and building tools that allow for red-teaming, while Daybreak Blue focuses on defensive tasks such as reviewing code, analyzing malware and investigating incidents. GPT-6 Cyber will initially be available to a select group of approved Daybreak Red customers only, with access expanding to all Red customers over the coming weeks, the company said. Separately, OpenAI said it is expanding early testing of Astra for defensive security work to more organizations and individual security researchers. through Daybreak Blue.

sources.name: TechCrunch AI
sources.title: OpenAI released a new cybersecurity model. Is that enough?
sources.text: Max Justicz, the chief technology officer and co-founder of the startup Charge Robotics, used an OpenAI model to find a severe vulnerability that — if exploited — could allow hackers to take control of servers running Ubuntu, a widely used open source Linux-based operating system. Justicz, who has a hobbyist’s interest in cybersecurity and previously found a vulnerability in the same codebase, told TechCrunch that he found this issue using GPT 5.6 Sol, released in July, through the AI maker’s Daybreak Blue, a program that gives cybersecurity defenders access to powerful frontier models. “I literally just aimed ChatGPT at the same body of code and said ‘I found this bug previously that was fixed several years ago, please find bugs as bad or worse,’ and it came back in two hours with this,” Justicz said. “It’s extremely convoluted and hard for a human to find, but it works!” He reported the issue to the Debian Project, which maintains the software in question and issued a patch to fix the vulnerability. There has been no known evidence of exploitation. Still, the ease with which he found it suggests that we’ve only seen the tip of the iceberg when it comes to potential exploits that even novice hackers can utilize with the help of AI models. “I can only imagine what one could do with more time and access to less neutered models. We should expect some extremely crazy bugs to be found and exploited over the next few months,” Justicz wrote in a social media thread discussing his finding. “This might be obvious to most folks here, but there is currently huge alpha in taking some code or binary someone has not audited yet and just aiming a powerful AI model at it.” OpenAI appears to have noticed. Today, the AI giant announced a new model focused on cybersecurity, ChatGPT Cyber, would be made available to the highest tier of users in the cybersecurity program, Daybreak Red, which allows offensive cybersecurity researchers tools for vulnerability hunting and development. Yesterday, OpenAI said that the same model had been used to scan and prepare patches for vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel, finding 948 potential issues. OpenAI also found 81 “novel” vulnerabilities in Firefox, the web browser. “Our goal is to dramatically expand Daybreak, bringing advanced security research to organizations of every size, independent researchers, and open-source maintainers,” the frontier lab said in a statement. OpenAI has insisted that there is a narrow window of time for the people who safeguard digital infrastructure to take action before AI models become even better at hacking and easier to access. For cyber defenders, however, it can feel like the frontier labs have unleashed a mountain of new work that outstrips their resources. Justicz said that he personally spent about $5,000 on subscriptions and tokens to find several exploits. Besides Daybreak’s model access, OpenAI has also announced a $1 billion initiative to support cybersecurity professionals in the program who work on critical infrastructure like the electrical grid or water systems. The Daybreak program has its own critiques. Justicz notes that the frontier lab appears to have recently “nerfed” Daybreak Blue to make it less useful at finding vulnerabilities. On one hand, it may be good to limit access from potential bad actors — Justicz said he just uploaded a photo of his driver’s license to join the program. On the other, cybersecurity professionals say they have one hand tied if they can’t use frontier technology while bad actors can deploy open-weight models with abliterated guardrails . Still, OpenAI says just “thousands” of cybersecurity professionals are participating in the Daybreak program, versus a far larger number of potential hackers. It’s unclear if frontier labs are devoting enough of their resources to this issue. Eric Wallace, a researcher on OpenAI’s technical staff, said that “we are now allocating a significant amount of our frontier compute towards discovering and patching vulnerabilities in open source codebases, fully pro bono.” But the Linux bug hunt cost $1.2 million, which is significantly less than the approximate $6 million token spend the company invested in finding a potential solution to a famous problem of fluid dynamics. If there is a narrow window of time to patch the digital infrastructure the world depends on, more urgency may be required.
